rules.rationale: Never block sources that are in the never‑block whitelist (loopback, OOB management, SVI gateways, management hosts, monitoring host, etc.). Blocking any of these IPs would partition the fabric or kill audit capability.
External (outside‑fabric) sources are never dropped by the agent; enforcement is performed by perimeter devices. The agent only logs such events.

All listed SIDs represent hard micro‑segmentation violations or malicious content (e.g., direct DB access from WEB, APP‑GW bypass, unauthorized zone‑to‑PAYMENTS, DB outbound exfil, C2 beacon, etc.). Dropping the source IP at flow scope contains the threat while preserving the rest of the fabric.

These signatures detect malicious payloads inside otherwise allowed DB traffic (SQL injection, destructive statements, COPY‑TO‑PROGRAM, unbounded SELECT burst). Even though the zone pair is ALLOW, the content semantics mandate DROP.
SID 9000052 indicates a high‑rate UDP flood; the response in the catalogue is DROP src_ip. Blocking the source contains the DDoS.
SID 9000062 flags DB‑tier outbound to external – a crown‑jewel exfiltration indicator. The catalogue response is DROP src_ip.
These signatures are informational, reconnaissance, flooding, or audit events. Policy calls for logging only; no traffic is blocked.
SID 9000012 fires on allowed DB connections as well; the response for allowed pairs is to log only, preserving legitimate traffic.
